requirements:
The system manages modification of cloud resources in an IAM environment.

The people involved are owners, developers, operators, and org admins. One person may hold both the owner and developer role at the same time.

The resources are cloud resources, secrets, and org units. Every cloud resource records its owner, org unit, tags, environment, and temporary grant.

Each requester carries their organization membership.

Each request carries source IP, whether MFA was used, and session age.

Owners, developers, and operators may modify a cloud resource only when MFA was used.

When MFA was not used, owners, developers, and operators must not modify a cloud resource.

Owners, developers, and operators may modify a cloud resource outside production, or in production when it has been promoted.

Owners, developers, and operators must not modify a production cloud resource that has not been promoted unless the requester belongs under that cloud resource's org unit.

When the requester belongs under the cloud resource's org unit, the production promotion requirement does not block the modification.

A request by an owner to modify a cloud resource that does not trip any prohibition above must be able to succeed.

The system manages document editing, review, and publication across an enterprise workspace.

The people involved are authors, editors, viewers, and compliance officers, and a single person may hold both the author and editor role at the same time.

The resources are documents and workspaces; every document records its owner, its share list, its classification, whether it carries a version lock, its labels, and its status, and every workspace records its members.

An author or editor may edit a document only while it is in draft status.

Once a document has left draft status, for example because it has been published, neither an author nor an editor may edit it.

An author or editor may edit a draft document only when the requester appears on that document's share list.

If the requester does not appear on the document's share list, neither an author nor an editor may edit the document, even while it is in draft status.

An author or editor may edit a draft document only when the document carries a version lock.

If a draft document does not carry a version lock, neither an author nor an editor may edit it, even if the requester is on the share list.

An author or editor must not edit a document unless it is in draft status, carries a version lock, and lists the requester on its share list.

A request by an author to edit a document that is in draft status, carries a version lock, and lists the author on its share list must be able to succeed.

The system manages personnel records, payroll work, and leave approvals.

The people involved are employees, managers, h r specialists, and payroll admins. One person may hold both the manager and employee role at the same time.

The resources are payroll runs, employee records, and leave requests. Every employee record records the employee, their manager, its PII level, and the department.

Each requester carries a clearance, and each request carries whether it is on the corporate VPN and the current time.

A manager or h r specialist may view an employee record only when their clearance dominates the record's PII level and the request is not on the corporate VPN.

When the request is on the corporate VPN, the clearance requirement does not block the manager or h r specialist from viewing the employee record.

A manager and an h r specialist must not view an employee record from outside the corporate VPN when their clearance does not dominate the record's PII level.

A payroll admin may prepare a payroll run.

A manager may approve a leave request.

A request by a manager to view an employee record that does not trip any prohibition above must be able to succeed.

The system manages the approval and release of bank wire transfers.
The people involved are originators, verifiers, treasury officers, and compliance reviewers. One person may hold both the originator and verifier roles at the same time.
The resources are wire transfers and accounts. Every wire transfer records who initiated it, who verified it, who screened it, its account, its amount, its fee, its amount tier, its beneficiary, its currency code, whether it is high risk, and its status. Every account records its holder and its allowed beneficiaries.
Each request carries the current time, the daily cutoff, whether it came from the secure network, whether multi-factor authentication was used, and whether an emergency has been declared.
In this workflow a wire is first approved and then released, and the release step can see the wire's status and who verified it as recorded by the earlier steps.
A person may approve a wire only when their authority tier is at least as high as the wire's amount tier, and a person whose authority tier is below the wire's amount tier may not approve it.
A wire may be approved only when its amount plus fee crosses the set threshold, and a request to approve one whose amount plus fee stays at or below that threshold is refused.
A wire may be released only after it has been verified, and a request to release one that has not been verified is refused.
A wire may be released only when its beneficiary is on the account's screened allowlist, and a request to release one to a beneficiary not on that allowlist is refused.
A wire may be released only when its amount crosses the set money threshold, and a request to release one whose amount stays at or below that threshold is refused.
Neither a verifier nor a treasury officer may approve a wire whose amount tier exceeds their authority tier.
A run through the workflow by a verifier whose authority tier is at least the wire's amount tier, where the amount plus fee crosses the threshold so the verifier approves it, and where a treasury officer then releases the verified wire to an allowlisted beneficiary for an amount above the money threshold, tripping no prohibition above, must be able to succeed.

The system manages patent applications, office actions, filings, and examination work on a prosecution docket.

The people involved are patent attorneys, docket clerks, examiners, and inventors. One person may hold both the patent attorney and docket clerk roles, and one person may hold both the examiner and inventor roles.

The resources are patent applications, office actions, and filings. Every patent application records its inventor, prosecuting attorney, assigned examiner, team, confidentiality, bar date, and status.

Each requester carries their clearance.

Each request carries the current date, whether it is made on the firm network, whether there is a court order, and whether MFA was used.

An examiner may examine a patent application only when MFA was used.

An examiner who has not used MFA must not examine a patent application.

An examiner who is a named inventor on a patent application must recuse and may not examine that application.

An examiner who is not a named inventor on the application and has used MFA may examine it.

A request by an examiner to examine an application that does not trip any prohibition above must be able to succeed.

The system manages employee expense reports and reimbursement disbursement.

The people involved are employees, line managers, finance reviewers, and controllers.

One person may hold both the employee and line manager role at the same time.

The resources are expense reports and reimbursements.

Every expense report records its submitter, approver, total amount, meal total, lodging total, category, amount tier, whether a receipt is attached, its status, and when it was submitted.

Every reimbursement records its expense report, who disbursed it, and the amount.

Each requester carries an approval tier.

Each request carries whether it is on the corporate network, the current time, and whether it is an emergency approval.

During business hours, a controller may disburse a reimbursement only when the expense report has approved status.

Outside business hours, the approved-report requirement does not bind the controller.

A controller must not disburse a reimbursement for an unapproved expense report during business hours.

A request by a controller to disburse a reimbursement that does not trip any prohibition above must be able to succeed.

The system manages outpatient controlled-substance dispensing.

The people involved are pharmacy technicians, staff pharmacists, pharmacists in charge, and prescribers. One person may hold both the staff pharmacist and pharmacist in charge role at the same time.

The resources are prescriptions and dispense records. Every prescription records its prescriber, patient, entered by, verified by, prescriber DEA, schedule level, refills remaining, and status.

Each requester carries dispense authority and a state license.

Each request carries whether PDMP was checked, whether MFA was used, whether it came from the pharmacy network, the current time, and whether emergency override was used.

A staff pharmacist or pharmacist in charge may verify a prescription only while it is in the received stage when no exception applies.

A staff pharmacist or pharmacist in charge who holds the particular exception role may verify a prescription outside the received stage.

A staff pharmacist or pharmacist in charge may verify a prescription outside the received stage when the refills remaining crosses the threshold.

A staff pharmacist and a pharmacist in charge must not verify a prescription outside the received stage when neither exception applies.

A request by a staff pharmacist to verify a prescription that does not trip any prohibition above must be able to succeed.

The system manages switching orders and field execution for electrical grid operations.
The people involved are planners, shift supervisors, operators, control room operators, and auditors.
One person may hold both the planner and shift supervisor roles, and one person may hold both the operator and control room operator roles.
The resources are switching orders and lockout tags.
Every switching order records its planner, executor, feeder, voltage level, circuit count, status, scheduled start, and scheduled end.
Every lockout tag records its order, who applied it, and the feeder.
Each request carries the current time, whether it is on the SCADA network, whether lockout tagout has been verified, and whether an outage emergency has been declared.
An operator or control room operator may execute switching only after the switching order has been authorized.
Neither an operator nor a control room operator may execute switching for an order that has not been authorized.
When the request falls within the order's scheduled switching window, the timing requirement is satisfied.
When the request falls outside the order's scheduled switching window, neither an operator nor a control room operator may execute the switching.
When the number of circuits being switched crosses the threshold for control-room handling, only a control room operator may execute the switching.
When the number of circuits being switched does not cross that threshold, an operator may execute the switching.
A request by an operator to execute a switching that does not trip any prohibition above must be able to succeed.

The system manages the review, signing, and execution of contracts through their lifecycle.
The people involved are drafters, reviewers, signatories, and contract administrators. One person may hold both the drafter and reviewer roles at the same time, and one person may hold both the reviewer and signatory roles at the same time.
The resources are contracts and signatures. Every contract records its drafter, its reviewer, its counterparty, its contract value, the authority tier it requires, its effective date, and its status. Every signature records the contract it is on, who signed it, and its amount.
Each request carries the current date, whether it came from the corporate network, whether multi-factor authentication was used, and whether an escalation has been approved.
In this workflow a contract is first reviewed, then signed, and then executed, and each later step can see the contract's status and who acted on it as recorded by the earlier steps.
A contract may be reviewed only while it is still in draft, and a request to review a contract that has left draft is refused.
A contract may be reviewed only when the reviewer is listed as conflicted against the contract's counterparty, and a request to review one from a reviewer not conflicted against its counterparty is refused.
A person may sign a contract only when their delegated authority tier is at least as high as the authority tier the contract requires, and a person whose authority tier is below what the contract requires may not sign it.
A contract may be signed only when the signatory is listed as conflicted against the contract's counterparty, and a request to sign one from a signatory not conflicted against its counterparty is refused.
A contract may be executed only after it has been signed, and a request to execute one that has not been signed is refused.
Neither a signatory nor a contract administrator may sign a contract whose required authority tier exceeds their delegated authority tier.
A run through the workflow by a reviewer conflicted against the counterparty who reviews a draft contract, where a signatory who is conflicted against the counterparty and has sufficient authority then signs it, and where a contract administrator then executes the signed contract, tripping no prohibition above, must be able to succeed.

The system manages classified document reading for an organization.
The people involved are analysts, officers, security admins, and contractors. One person may hold both the analyst and the officer role at the same time.
The resources are documents, dossiers, and access badges. Every document records its owner, its classification, its compartments, and its status.
Each requester carries their clearance, compartments, and nationality.
Each request carries whether it comes from the intranet and the current time.
When a document carries the relevant compartment label, an analyst or officer may read it only if their clearance dominates the document's classification.
When a document does not carry that compartment label, this classification comparison does not block the analyst or officer from reading it.
An analyst or officer may read a document only when the request comes from the intranet.
Neither an analyst nor an officer may read the document from outside the intranet.
A request by an analyst to read a document that does not trip any prohibition above must be able to succeed.

The system manages clear-to-close approval and fund disbursement for real-estate escrow files.

The people involved are escrow officers, senior escrow officers, escrow managers, title officers, and auditors. One person may hold both the escrow officer and senior escrow officer roles at the same time, or both the senior escrow officer and escrow manager roles at the same time.

The resources are escrow files and disbursements. Every escrow file records its escrow officer, its disbursement tier, the amount held, the number of payees, its file code, its region, its parties, its lien status, whether its title has been cleared, its status, and its closing date. Every disbursement records its escrow file, who authorized it, its amount, and when it was wired.

Each request carries the current time, whether it comes from the corporate network, whether dual control has been confirmed, and whether a settlement emergency has been declared.

An escrow officer may open an escrow file, and a title officer or an escrow manager may then approve that file clear to close.

An escrow officer who opened a file and who also serves as the approving title officer or escrow manager may not approve that same file clear to close, while a title officer or escrow manager who did not open the file may approve it.

A file may be approved clear to close only when its title has been cleared of encumbrances, while a request to approve a file whose title still carries encumbrances must be refused.

An auditor may only view the audit log and must not approve any file clear to close.

A request by a title officer to approve a clear to close for a file that trips none of the prohibitions above must be able to succeed.

The system manages course modules and gradebook records in a learning-management system.
The people involved are the instructor of record, teaching assistants, learners, and coordinators. One person may hold both the instructor of record and teaching assistant roles at the same time.
The resources are modules and grade entries. Every module records its course, instructor of record, roster, prerequisite level, release time, locked flag, and status, and every grade entry records its learner, module, poster, and status.
Each requester carries their completed level.
Each request carries the current time, whether it comes from the institution network, and the preview window.
An instructor of record, teaching assistant, learner, or coordinator may view a module only once it is released when the request is not on the institution network.
An instructor of record, teaching assistant, learner, or coordinator may view a draft or scheduled module when the request is on the institution network.
An instructor of record, teaching assistant, learner, or coordinator must not view a draft or scheduled module when the request is not on the institution network.
A request by an instructor of record to view a module that does not trip any prohibition above must be able to succeed.

The system manages student records and grades for an educational institution.

The people involved are instructors, students, parents, and the registrar. One person may hold both the instructor and the parent role at the same time.

The resources are student records, grades, and courses. Every student record records the student, the advisor, the student's age, any FERPA directory-information block, and the status.

Every grade records the student, the course, the person who graded it, and the status.

Every course records its instructor and roster.

Each request carries the current date and whether it comes from the campus network.

An instructor, student, or parent must not view a withdrawn student's record when a FERPA directory-information block is set.

A registrar may view a withdrawn student's record when a FERPA directory-information block is set.

When no FERPA directory-information block is set, this withdrawn-student viewing limit does not apply.

A request by an instructor to view a student record that does not trip any prohibition above must be able to succeed.

The system manages namespace-scoped role-based access control for a Kubernetes platform, including the issuing and revoking of service-account tokens.

The people involved are deployers, maintainers, cluster operators, and service accounts. One person may hold both the deployer and maintainer roles at the same time.

The resources are namespaces, workloads, namespace secrets, and service-account tokens.

Every namespace records its members, its team group, and its environment.

Every workload records its namespace, its creator, the verb it requires, its replica count, its labels, and its environment.

Every namespace secret records its namespace, its owner, its sensitivity, and its status.

Every service-account token records its subject, the namespace it is bound to, the cluster operator who issued it, its expiration time, and its status.

Each requester carries a clearance level, a granted scope, and a record of the team groups they belong to.

A cluster operator may revoke a service-account token.

The cluster operator who issued a given service-account token must be the same cluster operator who revokes it.

This same-operator requirement applies only when the requester belongs under the token's bound-namespace team group.

If a cluster operator does not belong under the token's bound-namespace team group, that operator may not revoke the token even if they were the one who originally issued it.

Deployers, maintainers, and service accounts must not revoke any service-account token, since only cluster operators are permitted to perform that action.

A request by the cluster operator who issued a given token, made while that operator belongs under the token's bound-namespace team group, to revoke that token must be able to succeed.

The system manages smart-building automation and zone control.

The people involved are facility managers, zone controllers, maintenance techs, and tenants. One person may hold both the facility manager and zone controller role at the same time.

The resources are actuators, zones, and commission requests. Every actuator records its owner, zone group, device tags, maintenance flag, and status, every zone records its controller, criticality, and status, and every commission request records its device, requester, and status.

Each requester carries a control tier and membership information.

Each request carries the current time, whether occupancy is detected, whether it comes from the on-site building network, and whether there is a maintenance override.

A facility manager may approve a commission request only while it is in requested status.

A facility manager must not approve a commission request that is not in requested status.

A facility manager may approve a commission request only when the request comes from the on-site building network, and must not approve it from any other network.

A facility manager may approve a commission request only when the request falls within a permitted window, and must not approve it outside that window.

A request by a facility manager to approve a commission that does not trip any prohibition above must be able to succeed.

The system manages invoice approval and payment.

The people involved are clerks, approvers, finance managers, and auditors. One person may hold both the clerk and the approver role at the same time.

The resources are invoices, which record their creator, approver, amount, surcharge, line item count, status, cost center, and submission time, and payments, which record their invoice, issuer, and amount.

Each request carries the current time, whether it comes from the corporate network, and whether an emergency has been declared.

During business hours, an approver or finance manager may approve an invoice only after it has been submitted when its line item count does not cross the threshold.

When an invoice's line item count crosses the threshold, the submitted-status requirement does not apply.

Outside business hours, the business-hours approval rule does not bind.

An approver or finance manager must not approve an unsubmitted invoice during business hours when its line item count does not cross the threshold.

A request by an approver to approve an invoice that does not trip any prohibition above must be able to succeed.

The system manages the dispatch of carrier shipments and the confirmation of their delivery.

The people involved are planners, drivers, dispatch managers, depot supervisors, and auditors. One person may hold both the planner and the dispatch manager role at the same time.

The resources are shipments and delivery receipts. Every shipment records its planner, its driver of record, its piece count, its gross weight in kilograms, its status, its tracking code, its origin depot, its hazmat class, and the end of its delivery window. Every delivery receipt records its shipment, its recipient, and when it was signed.

Each request carries the current time, whether it comes from the depot network, whether the shipment has been declared expedited, and whether proof of delivery is present.

In this workflow a shipment is first dispatched and then its delivery is confirmed, and the confirmation step can see the shipment's status and its driver of record as recorded by the dispatch step.

A driver or dispatch manager may dispatch a shipment, but the person who planned the shipment may not be the driver of record who dispatches it, keeping planning and dispatch in different hands.

However, the planner may be the dispatching driver of record when the request originates on the origin depot's network.

The planner may likewise dispatch the shipment when its tracking code carries the assigned carrier prefix.

The same driver of record who dispatched a shipment must be the one to confirm its delivery, and a driver or depot supervisor who was not the dispatching driver of record may not confirm the delivery.

However, a driver or depot supervisor other than the dispatching driver of record may confirm the delivery when the confirmation is submitted from a depot network.

A run through the workflow by a driver who dispatches a shipment they did not plan and then confirms its delivery, tripping no prohibition above, must be able to succeed.

The system manages schedule overrides for zones and their actuators in a smart building automation platform.

The people involved are facility managers, zone controllers, maintenance technicians, and tenants, and one person may hold both the facility manager and zone controller roles at the same time.

The resources are actuators, zones, and commission requests: every actuator records its owner, zone group, device tags, maintenance flag, and status; every zone records its assigned controller, criticality level, and status; every commission request records the device involved, who requested it, and its status.

Each requester carries a control tier ranging from level 1 through level 4 and a list of the groups they belong to.

A zone controller or facility manager may override a zone's schedule only when their control tier dominates that zone's criticality level, so a control tier of 3 can override a zone rated critical while a control tier of 1 cannot.

A zone controller may override a zone's schedule only when they are that zone's assigned controller, and a zone controller who is assigned to a different zone must not override this zone's schedule.

A facility manager may override a zone's schedule only when they also currently hold the zone controller role, and a facility manager who does not hold the zone controller role must not override any zone's schedule.

A schedule may be overridden only when the zone's status is not locked, and when the zone's status is locked no override may take effect no matter how high the requester's control tier is.

Neither a zone controller nor a facility manager may override a zone's schedule unless the tier, assignment, role, and lock requirements above are all satisfied, and a maintenance technician or tenant must never override a zone's schedule under any circumstances.

A request by a zone controller who is that zone's assigned controller, whose control tier dominates the zone's criticality level, and whose zone is not locked, to override that zone's schedule must be able to succeed.

The system manages the review and execution of commercial leases at a real-estate brokerage.

The people involved are leasing agents, transaction coordinators, brokers, compliance officers, and auditors. One person may hold both the leasing agent and transaction coordinator roles at the same time, and one person may hold both the broker and compliance officer roles at the same time.

The resources are leases and executed leases, where every lease records its listing agent, the broker who reviewed it, its lease code, its monthly rent, its term in months, its square footage, its region, its premises class, its contingencies, its market segment, whether it is under a fair-housing hold, its status, and the close of its signing window.

Each request carries the current time, whether it comes from the brokerage network, whether the counterparty's identity has been verified, and whether a court order has been declared.

A leasing agent may draft a lease, moving it into the drafted state, and an auditor may view the audit log.

The listing agent who drafted a lease may not be the person who reviews it, and someone who did not draft the lease is free to review it.

This independence requirement applies only when the total contract value, the monthly rent multiplied by the term in months, crosses the high-value threshold, and when the total contract value stays at or below that threshold the requirement does not bind.

The independence requirement is relaxed when the leased square footage crosses the large-premises threshold, so on a large-premises lease the person who listed it may also review it; on a smaller lease the person who listed it may not review it.

A lease may be reviewed only by someone who holds the broker role required for licensed review, and a reviewer who does not hold that broker role may not review it.

When a court order has been declared, a broker may review a lease they themselves listed, setting aside the separation between listing and reviewing; without a declared court order, that separation stands.

If these two rules disagree on a single review, the court-order directive wins over the separation between listing and reviewing.

Absent both a declared court order and a large-premises footprint, neither a broker nor a transaction coordinator who listed a high-value lease may review it, and no one lacking the required broker role may review it.

A request by a licensed broker to review a high-value lease that they did not draft, tripping no prohibition above, must be able to succeed.

The system manages pages in an internal company wiki.

The people involved are contributors, reviewers, space admins, and readers. One person may hold both the contributor and reviewer role at the same time.

The resources are pages and spaces. Every page records its author, reviewer, space, classification, whether external sharing is enabled, labels, and status.

Each requester carries their clearance and space memberships.

Each request carries whether it is on the corporate network, the current time, and whether emergency access is being used.

A reader, contributor, reviewer, or space admin may view a page only when their clearance is high enough for the page's classification.

A reader, contributor, reviewer, or space admin who authored a page may view their own page even when their clearance is not high enough for the page's classification.

A reader, contributor, reviewer, or space admin may view a page only when the page is not archived.

A reader, contributor, reviewer, or space admin must not view an archived page.

A request by a reader to view a page that does not trip any prohibition above must be able to succeed.
